facts.raw_span: a 2-year history of a mildly pruritic, erythematous, and gradually enlarging lesion on the proximal portion of his left calf
the lesion had appeared without an identifiable cause
no improvement with topical corticosteroids and antifungals for the previous 2 months
ill-defined, nonindurated, erythematous-violaceous plaque that was slightly raised but with an atrophic appearance
Band-like vascular proliferation in the upper dermis with no grenz zone
Round vascular spaces lined by a single layer of endothelial cells
No hemosiderin deposits found with Perls Prussian blue stain
Vascular channel endothelial cells were positive for CD34 and CD31 but negative for D2-40
Ill-defined, erythematous-violaceous plaque with an atrophic appearance
Band-like vascular proliferation in the upper dermis with no grenz zone (hematoxylin-eosin)
Round vascular channels lined by a single layer of endothelial cells without atypia (hematoxylin-eosin)
CD34 immunostaining labels endothelial cells

concepts.why: The presence of band-like vascular proliferation in the upper dermis with no grenz zone, round vascular spaces lined by a single layer of endothelial cells, and positive CD34 and CD31 immunostaining are characteristic of Kaposi's Sarcoma.
The presence of band-like vascular proliferation in the upper dermis with no grenz zone and round vascular channels lined by a single layer of endothelial cells are also consistent with Angiosarcoma.
The presence of an ill-defined, erythematous-violaceous plaque with an atrophic appearance and band-like vascular proliferation in the upper dermis are also consistent with Hemangioma.
The presence of an ill-defined, erythematous-violaceous plaque with an atrophic appearance and lack of response to topical corticosteroids and antifungals are also consistent with Pyogenic Granuloma.

The presence of an ill-defined, erythematous-violaceous plaque with an atrophic appearance and lack of response to topical corticosteroids and antifungals are also consistent with Bacillary Angiomatosis.
The presence of an ill-defined, erythematous-violaceous plaque with an atrophic appearance is also consistent with Dermatofibroma.

The presence of band-like vascular proliferation in the upper dermis with no grenz zone and round vascular spaces lined by a single layer of endothelial cells are also consistent with Vascular Malformation.
The presence of band-like vascular proliferation in the upper dermis with no grenz zone and round vascular spaces lined by a single layer of endothelial cells are also consistent with Lymphangioma.

The absence of hemosiderin deposits, as indicated by the negative Perls Prussian blue stain, points towards Kaposi-like Lymphangiomatosis, which can present with similar histopathological features but lacks the characteristic hemosiderin deposits often seen in other vascular lesions.
